dominant_strengths: Iconic Things app icon anchors the page with strong macOS-native craft and instantly communicates product identity
Restrained palette of soft gray-blue background with confident blue accents reads cleanly and feels Apple-native
Clear typographic hierarchy: bold wordmark, calm body copy, and a single inviting CTA keep focus tight
dominant_weaknesses: Massive vertical whitespace below the fold makes the hero feel underpopulated rather than intentionally airy
Composition is dead-center and static — no secondary content, screenshots, or download CTA to drive behavior
Diagonal slice at the bottom appears arbitrary, breaking the otherwise calm grid without a clear payoff
fix_priorities: Add a primary download/CTA button beside the video link to convert the hero into an actionable landing
Introduce a product screenshot or app preview to balance the icon and demonstrate the interface
Tighten vertical spacing or add a secondary feature row so the page doesn't feel half-finished
Refine the diagonal divider into a meaningful section transition with content beneath it
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral appeal from the polished icon outweighs behavioral utility (weak CTA) and reflective depth (no story or differentiation beyond the tagline).
rationale.intent_fit: It reads unmistakably as the Things3 marketing page and honors the brand, but underdelivers as a conversion-focused Mac app landing.
